service_boundary: Represents OpenRouter's API routing service, not the upstream providers, the underlying model releases, or OpenRouter's end-user chat interface.
regional_controls: Enterprise customers can use documented EU in-region routing; provider and endpoint selection otherwise determines where upstream processing occurs.
retention_controls: OpenRouter documents opt-in prompt logging and per-request controls that restrict routing by upstream retention or data-collection policy; upstream provider behavior remains part of the effective boundary.
routing: Requests can use ordered providers, fallbacks, allowlists, denylists, privacy requirements, price ceilings, and latency or throughput preferences.
customization: The public service focuses on routing existing models and provider endpoints; private customer endpoints are documented separately as an enterprise beta and are not treated as a stable catalog capability here.
strengths: A single compatible API can express fallback, cost, latency, throughput, and data-policy constraints across providers.
Endpoint-level retention metadata makes privacy part of routing rather than a provider-wide assumption.
tradeoffs: Requests cross an additional service boundary before reaching an upstream inference provider.
Effective terms, availability, and data handling depend on both OpenRouter and the selected upstream endpoint.
